c08fcb72ab0c.en: In 1951, Claude Shannon played a game with English. He took a sentence, hid it, and asked a person to guess it, one letter at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> A wrong guess, and they guessed again, until they got it. Under each letter, he wrote down how many guesses it took.
c08fcb72ab0c.zh: 1951年，克劳德·香农和英语玩了一个游戏。他拿来一个句子，把它遮住，请一个人一个字母一个字母地猜。<bookmark mark='a'/>猜错了，就再猜，直到猜对为止。每个字母下面，他都记下猜了几次。

4b473668d3fa.en: Most letters fall on the first guess. <bookmark mark='a'/> Once you've seen m, o, t, o, r, c, y, the rest of motorcycle is free. <bookmark mark='b'/> The guesses pile up at a few places, mostly where a new word begins. That is where the information is.
4b473668d3fa.zh: 大多数字母，第一次就猜中了。<bookmark mark='a'/>一旦看到了m, o, t, o, r, c, y，motorcycle剩下的部分就不用猜了。<bookmark mark='b'/>猜测次数集中在少数几个地方，大多是一个新词开始的地方。信息就藏在那里。

09e4443ae401.en: From counts like these, Shannon estimated that English carries about one bit per letter, a bit being the answer to one yes-or-no question: between 0.6 and 1.3, <bookmark mark='a'/> when a letter guessed blindly could carry 4.75. Most of what we write is predictable.
09e4443ae401.zh: 根据这样的计数，香农估算出，英语每个字母大约携带1比特信息，所谓1比特，就是一个是或否问题的答案：在0.6到1.3之间，<bookmark mark='a'/>而一个盲猜的字母，最多可以携带4.75比特。我们写下的东西，大部分是可以预测的。

745b90b717f9.en: Shannon didn't start from nothing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Telegraphers knew that common letters deserve short codes: Morse gives e a single dot. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1928 Ralph Hartley, at Bell Labs, measured information by the logarithm of the number of possible messages. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1948 Shannon made it a theory: entropy, the bit, and the limits of compression. <bookmark mark='d'/> The guessing game, Huffman's code and arithmetic coding followed. <bookmark mark='e'/> Half a century later, the same game became how machines learn language: a network guessing the next word, in 2003, then GPT-2, and today's models.
745b90b717f9.zh: 香农并不是从零开始的。<bookmark mark='a'/>电报员早就知道，常见的字母应该用短的编码：摩尔斯电码给e的只是一个点。<bookmark mark='b'/>1928年，贝尔实验室的拉尔夫·哈特利，用可能消息个数的对数来衡量信息。<bookmark mark='c'/>1948年，香农把它变成了一门理论：熵，比特，以及压缩的极限。<bookmark mark='d'/>接着是猜字游戏、霍夫曼编码和算术编码。<bookmark mark='e'/>半个世纪之后，同一个游戏成了机器学习语言的方式：2003年，一个猜下一个词的神经网络；然后是GPT-2，以及今天的模型。

28b4df9b7785.en: Seventy-five years on, Shannon's game is exactly what large language models are trained to play. Give one the start of a sentence, <bookmark mark='a'/> and it returns a probability for every possible next word. <bookmark mark='b'/> GPT-2, from 2019, with a hundred and twenty-four million parameters, the adjustable numbers inside it, gives the word Paris 6 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Qwen3, a 2025 model with four billion, gives the word Paris 35 percent.
28b4df9b7785.zh: 75年过去了，香农的游戏正是大语言模型被训练去玩的游戏。给它一个句子的开头，<bookmark mark='a'/>它就为每一个可能的下一个词给出一个概率。<bookmark mark='b'/>2019年的GPT-2，有1.24亿个参数，也就是模型里那些可调的数，给Paris这个词6%的概率。<bookmark mark='c'/>2025年的Qwen3，有40亿个参数，给Paris这个词35%的概率。

a3893008dd6d.en: Strictly, a model guesses the next token. <bookmark mark='a'/> A token is the chunk of text it guesses at one time: a word, a piece of a word, or a punctuation mark. Here is a line of a 1930 novel, cut the way GPT-2 cuts it.
a3893008dd6d.zh: 严格地说，模型猜的是下一个词元。<bookmark mark='a'/>词元，就是模型一次猜出的一小块文本：一个词，一个词的一部分，或者一个标点符号。这是一部1930年小说里的一行，按GPT-2的方式切开。

410fa38cd482.en: Which raises the question this whole series is about. What do you have to know, to guess well?
410fa38cd482.zh: 这就引出了整个系列要回答的问题：要猜得好，你得知道些什么？

5c11d4fb5650.en: Over thirty-one parts, we'll build the answer from the ground up: <bookmark mark='a'/> foundations, <bookmark mark='b'/> learning from data, <bookmark mark='c'/> transformers, <bookmark mark='d'/> generation and perception, <bookmark mark='e'/> agency and reasoning, <bookmark mark='f'/> and finally, looking inside, and whether we can trust it.
5c11d4fb5650.zh: 在31个部分里，我们会从头搭建出这个答案：<bookmark mark='a'/>基础，<bookmark mark='b'/>从数据中学习，<bookmark mark='c'/>Transformer，<bookmark mark='d'/>生成与感知，<bookmark mark='e'/>能动性与推理，<bookmark mark='f'/>最后，往模型里面看，以及我们能不能信任它。

33ce58bd2a7d.en: Part one starts where Shannon did. <bookmark mark='a'/> What information is, and why it's measured in bits; the best codes, and Shannon's limit; the price of a wrong model; a code that turns any guesser into a compressor; how a model learns to guess; and how far guessing has come. Guessing well and compressing well, we'll see, are the same thing.
33ce58bd2a7d.zh: 第1部分从香农出发的地方开始。<bookmark mark='a'/>信息是什么，为什么用比特来衡量；最好的编码，以及香农的极限；错误模型的代价；一种能把任何猜测者变成压缩器的编码；模型怎样学会猜；以及猜测已经走了多远。我们会看到，猜得好和压缩得好，是同一件事。

c226dcca3f97.en: Chapter one. Before we can score a guess, we need a way to write one down.
c226dcca3f97.zh: 第1章。在给猜测打分之前，我们得先有办法把猜测写下来。

352a7e0aea44.en: Take 30 novels, from Pride and Prejudice to The Great Gatsby, and count every symbol: Shannon's alphabet of twenty-six letters and the space, capitals and punctuation dropped. That's <bookmark mark='a'/> 22.8 million symbols. <bookmark mark='b'/> The most common is the space, about one symbol in 5. Then e, one in 10.
352a7e0aea44.zh: 拿来30部小说，从《傲慢与偏见》到《了不起的盖茨比》，数一数每一个符号：用香农的字母表，26个字母加空格，大写和标点都去掉。一共是<bookmark mark='a'/>22.8百万个符号。<bookmark mark='b'/>最常见的是空格，大约每5个符号里有一个。其次是e，每10个里有一个。

37e810f0eb03.en: Sorted, the familiar order appears: space, e, t, a, o, n. <bookmark mark='z'/> The rarest, z, turns up about once in 1,900 symbols.
37e810f0eb03.zh: 排好序，熟悉的顺序就出现了：空格、e、t、a、o、n。<bookmark mark='z'/>最少见的z，大约每1900个符号才出现一次。

396f9e341287.en: This is a probability distribution: a number for each possibility, <bookmark mark='a'/> none negative, adding up to one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stack the bars end to end, and they fill a bar of length one, a sliver per symbol, as wide as its probability. A guess, written down, shares one unit of belief among the possibilities.
396f9e341287.zh: 这就是一个概率分布：每种可能都有一个数，<bookmark mark='a'/>没有负的，加起来等于1。<bookmark mark='b'/>把这些柱子首尾相接，它们填满一根长度为1的条，每个符号一小段，宽度就是它的概率。一个写下来的猜测，就是把一个单位的信念，分给各种可能。

26a5bcc2f931.en: But we rarely guess from nothing. Once you know the previous letter, the odds change. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the whole table: each row is a previous symbol, each square how likely the next one is. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is conditional probability: B given A is the probability of both, divided by that of A.
26a5bcc2f931.zh: 不过，我们很少凭空去猜。一旦知道了前一个字母，可能性就变了。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是整张表：每一行是一个前一个符号，每个小方格表示下一个符号有多大可能。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是条件概率：已知A时B的概率，等于两者同时发生的概率，除以A的概率。

e8c835c1c0cb.en: In our books, q appears 18,496 times, and all but 27 are followed by u. <bookmark mark='a'/> So u given q is 0.9985. <bookmark mark='b'/> After a space, though, almost anything can come next: a new word is starting.
e8c835c1c0cb.zh: 在我们的书里，q出现了18496次，除了27次之外，后面跟的都是u。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以已知q时u的概率是0.9985。<bookmark mark='b'/>可在空格之后，几乎什么都可能出现：一个新词正要开始。

b75ed09f47f7.en: Multiply that definition out, and you get a rule for whole strings. <bookmark mark='a'/> The probability of two symbols is the probability of the first, times the probability of the second given the first. <bookmark mark='b'/> For three, treat the first two as a single event, <bookmark mark='c'/> and substitute.
b75ed09f47f7.zh: 把这个定义乘开，就得到一条关于整串符号的规则。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个符号的概率，等于第一个的概率，乘以已知第一个时第二个的概率。<bookmark mark='b'/>三个的时候，把前两个看成一个事件，<bookmark mark='c'/>再代进去。

79b17b160180.en: And so on, one symbol at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> A whole text's probability is a product of next-symbol guesses, each knowing everything before it. This is the chain rule, and it is exact: no assumption made. <bookmark mark='b'/> It's why a machine that only guesses the next symbol can score, or write, a whole text.
79b17b160180.zh: 依此类推，一次一个符号。<bookmark mark='a'/>一整段文本的概率，就是一连串对下一个符号的猜测的乘积，每次猜测都知道前面的一切。这就是链式法则，而且它是精确的：没有做任何假设。<bookmark mark='b'/>这也是为什么一台只会猜下一个符号的机器，能给一整段文本打分，甚至写出一整段文本。

958186296635.en: Here's the chain rule as a picture. Someone has written, he said, and we want the chance that the next three letters are t, h, e. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first bar shares the whole unit of belief among the 27 next symbols, given the last three: i, d, space. t gets a sliver 0.155 wide.
958186296635.zh: 这是链式法则的一幅图。有人刚写下he said，我们想知道接下来三个字母是t、h、e的可能性。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一根条把整整一个单位的信念，按最后三个符号i、d、空格，分给27个可能的下一个符号。t分到的一段，宽0.155。

0165150a061a.en: Now zoom into that sliver and share it out again, <bookmark mark='a'/> by the probabilities after d, space, t. h takes 61 percent of it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Zoom again: after space, t, h, e takes 70 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> The final sliver's width is the product, 0.0666: the probability of the whole string.
0165150a061a.zh: 现在放大这一小段，再分一次，<bookmark mark='a'/>按d、空格、t之后的概率来分。h占了其中的61%。<bookmark mark='b'/>再放大：在空格、t、h之后，e占了70%。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后这一小段的宽度就是它们的乘积，0.0666：也就是整串的概率。

8fd1c5226e48.en: Keep this picture in mind: nested slivers, each one a guess. In chapter eight, it becomes a way to compress text.
8fd1c5226e48.zh: 记住这幅图：一层套一层的小段，每一层都是一次猜测。到第8章，它会变成一种压缩文本的方法。

1530771f7664.en: Chapter two. How surprised should you be?

a137f7df111a.en: If you were sure something would happen, seeing it happen tells you nothing. <bookmark mark='a'/> u after q: no news. <bookmark mark='b'/> A coin landing heads tells you a little. <bookmark mark='c'/> A letter e, a bit more. <bookmark mark='d'/> And a z, which turns up about once in 1,900 symbols, tells you a lot. The less likely it was, the more you learn.
a137f7df111a.zh: 如果你确信某件事会发生，看到它发生，什么也学不到。<bookmark mark='a'/>q后面的u：不是新闻。<bookmark mark='b'/>硬币正面朝上，告诉你一点点。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个字母e，多一点。<bookmark mark='d'/>而一个z，大约每1900个符号才出现一次，告诉你很多。它越不可能，你学到的就越多。

62203ad93034.en: Let's turn that into mathematics. Call the surprise of an event with probability p, s of p. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ask a few modest things. It depends only on p. <bookmark mark='b'/> It goes down as p goes up, and a certain event is no surprise at all. <bookmark mark='c'/> For independent events, where one tells you nothing about the other, probabilities multiply and surprises should add: <bookmark mark='d'/> heads on a coin and a five on a die, together, as surprising as the two added up. <bookmark mark='e'/> And small changes in p make small changes in s.
62203ad93034.zh: 我们把这个想法变成数学。把概率为p的事件的意外度记作s(p)。<bookmark mark='a'/>提几条很朴素的要求。它只取决于p。<bookmark mark='b'/>p越大，它越小，一件必然发生的事，毫不意外。<bookmark mark='c'/>对独立事件，也就是知道其中一个，对另一个毫无帮助，它们的概率相乘，意外度应该相加：<bookmark mark='d'/>硬币正面朝上，同时骰子掷出5，这两件事一起的意外度，等于两者之和。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有，p的微小变化，只带来s的微小变化。

7a8c06f1980d.en: Remarkably, those rules leave only one choice. Measure probabilities in halvings: <bookmark mark='a'/> write p as two to the minus x, and let g of x be its surprise. <bookmark mark='b'/> Rule three says g turns sums into sums. <bookmark mark='c'/> So g of n is n times g of one, for every whole number, <bookmark mark='d'/> and for every fraction. <bookmark mark='e'/> Continuity fills in the rest: g of x is x times g of one.
7a8c06f1980d.zh: 了不起的是，这几条要求只留下一种选择。用对半分的次数来衡量概率：<bookmark mark='a'/>把p写成2的负x次方，令g(x)为它的意外度。<bookmark mark='b'/>第3条说，g把和变成和。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以对每个正整数n，g(n)等于n乘以g(1)，<bookmark mark='d'/>对每个分数也一样。<bookmark mark='e'/>连续性补上其余的数：g(x)等于x乘以g(1)。

ba1aa45867f4.en: Put the probability back in, and the surprise must be a constant times the log of one over p. <bookmark mark='a'/> The constant just picks a unit. Let a fair coin flip carry exactly one, and call it a bit: an event of probability p carries log, base two, of one over p, bits.
ba1aa45867f4.zh: 把概率代回去，意外度就必须是一个常数乘以p分之1的对数。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个常数只是选定一个单位。让一次公平的抛硬币恰好携带一个单位，把它叫作比特：概率为p的事件，携带以2为底、p分之1的对数那么多比特。

5272e07fb24b.en: Here's that function. <bookmark mark='a'/> A coin: one bit. A face of a die: 2.58 bits. <bookmark mark='b'/> The letter e: 3.32 bits. The letter z: 10.9. <bookmark mark='c'/> And u, right after q: 0.002 bits, almost nothing. <bookmark mark='d'/> As p heads to zero, the surprise grows without limit.
5272e07fb24b.zh: 这就是那个函数。<bookmark mark='a'/>一枚硬币：1比特。骰子的一面：2.58比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>字母e：3.32比特。字母z：10.9。<bookmark mark='c'/>而紧跟在q后面的u：0.002比特，几乎为零。<bookmark mark='d'/>当p趋向于零，意外度会无限增大。

53d11afd5ded.en: And because logs turn products into sums, the chain rule turns into something lovely. <bookmark mark='a'/> A whole text's surprise is the sum of its symbols' surprises, each given everything before it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is Shannon's sentence again, each letter's surprise a bar, judged by a model that knows only the previous 5 letters.
53d11afd5ded.zh: 因为对数把乘积变成和，链式法则就变成了一个很漂亮的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>一整段文本的意外度，等于它每个符号的意外度之和，每个符号都是在已知前面一切的条件下。<bookmark mark='b'/>这又是香农的那个句子，每个字母的意外度是一根柱子，评判它的模型只知道前面5个字母。

d8d892eb08c1.en: The tall bars are where the text surprised the model: the starts of words, and words it didn't expect. <bookmark mark='a'/> Altogether, 182 bits for 101 symbols: 1.8 bits per symbol, under half of the 4.08 bits the letter frequencies alone would give. Remember that number; it's how we'll keep score.
d8d892eb08c1.zh: 高的柱子，就是文本让模型意外的地方：词的开头，以及它没料到的词。<bookmark mark='a'/>加起来，101个符号共182比特：每个符号1.8比特，不到只用字母频率时4.08比特的一半。记住这个数，我们就靠它来记分。

fb384d41c8d0.en: Surprise is about one event. Before it happens, we can ask: on average, how surprised should we expect to be? <bookmark mark='a'/> Weight each surprise by how often it happens, and add up. That average is the entropy, H of p.
fb384d41c8d0.zh: 意外度说的是一个事件。在它发生之前，我们可以问：平均来说，我们预计会有多意外？<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个意外度按它出现的频率加权，再加起来。这个平均值就是熵，记作H(p)。

97360eb6aad3.en: There's a nice picture of it. Take the unit bar from chapter one, <bookmark mark='a'/> a sliver per symbol, as wide as its probability, common to rare. <bookmark mark='b'/> Raise each sliver to the height of its surprise: common symbols wide and low, rare ones thin and tall. <bookmark mark='c'/> The entropy is the total area: for English letters, 4.08 bits.
97360eb6aad3.zh: 它有一幅很好的图。拿出第1章那根单位长度的条，<bookmark mark='a'/>每个符号一小段，宽度是它的概率，从常见到罕见。<bookmark mark='b'/>把每一小段升高到它的意外度那么高：常见的符号又宽又矮，罕见的又窄又高。<bookmark mark='c'/>熵就是总面积：英语字母是4.08比特。

1746f60f8188.en: The simplest case is a coin. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fair, it has one bit of entropy. <bookmark mark='b'/> Bias it, and it gets easier to guess: heads ninety percent of the time, 0.47 bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Always heads: no entropy at all. Entropy is largest when the outcomes are equally likely.
1746f60f8188.zh: 最简单的情形是一枚硬币。<bookmark mark='a'/>公平的硬币，熵是1比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>让它有偏向，就更容易猜：90%的时候正面朝上，0.47比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>总是正面朝上：完全没有熵。各种结果同样可能时，熵最大。

6d2846dbfd93.en: We built entropy out of surprise; Shannon went the other way. In 1948 he asked what any measure of uncertainty should satisfy. <bookmark mark='a'/> It should change continuously with the probabilities. <bookmark mark='b'/> With n equally likely outcomes, more outcomes, more uncertainty. <bookmark mark='c'/> And a choice broken into two successive choices should cost the first choice, plus the second, weighted by how often you face it. <bookmark mark='d'/> His example: a half, a third, a sixth is a fair coin, then, half the time, two thirds against one third.
6d2846dbfd93.zh: 我们是用意外度搭出熵的；香农走的是另一条路。1948年，他问：任何一种不确定性的度量，应该满足什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>它应该随概率连续地变化。<bookmark mark='b'/>有n种同样可能的结果时，结果越多，不确定性越大。<bookmark mark='c'/>一次选择被拆成先后两次选择时，不确定性应该等于第一次选择的，加上第二次选择的，按你遇到第二次选择的频率加权。<bookmark mark='d'/>他的例子：二分之一、三分之一、六分之一，等于先抛一枚公平的硬币，然后有一半的时候，再在三分之二和三分之一之间选一次。

7688608c5bd4.en: Our letters work the same way. <bookmark mark='a'/> First choose space, vowel or consonant: 1.48 bits. Then choose which one: 2.20 bits among the vowels, 3.85 among the consonants. <bookmark mark='b'/> Weighted and added, that's 4.08 bits: the entropy of the letters, exactly.
7688608c5bd4.zh: 我们的字母也是这样。<bookmark mark='a'/>先选空格、元音还是辅音：1.48比特。再选具体是哪一个：元音里2.20比特，辅音里3.85比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>加权相加，得到4.08比特：恰好就是字母的熵。

5266523d02b1.en: And he proved nothing else meets them. Call A of n the uncertainty of n equal choices. <bookmark mark='a'/> Choosing among s to the m equal outcomes is m choices among s in a row, so by the third requirement, A of s to the m is m times A of s. <bookmark mark='b'/> Squeeze any number between powers of another, and the second forces A of n to be a constant times log n. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now take probabilities that are fractions, n i over N: choose one of N equal outcomes in two steps, the block, then the outcome inside it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Solve for H, <bookmark mark='e'/> and out comes minus K, sum of p log p; continuity covers the rest.
5266523d02b1.zh: 他还证明了，别的什么都满足不了这些要求。把n个同样可能的选择的不确定性记作A(n)。<bookmark mark='a'/>在s的m次方个同样可能的结果里选一个，等于连续在s个里选m次，所以按第三条要求，A(s的m次方)等于m乘以A(s)。<bookmark mark='b'/>把任何一个数夹在另一个数的两个幂之间，第二条要求就迫使A(n)等于一个常数乘以log n。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在看是分数的概率，n i除以N：从N个同样可能的结果里选一个，分两步，先选块，再选块里的那一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>解出H，<bookmark mark='e'/>得到的就是负K乘以p log p之和；其余的由连续性补上。

501be18d627b.en: Up to a unit, entropy is the only consistent measure of uncertainty. That's why every part of this series measures information this way.
501be18d627b.zh: 除了单位的选择，熵是唯一自洽的不确定性度量。这就是为什么这个系列的每一部分，都用这种方式来衡量信息。

8074f9664d62.en: In general, with K outcomes, the entropy is at most log two of K. <bookmark mark='a'/> The proof is one inequality. The log bends downward, so the average of logs is at most the log of the average: Jensen's inequality. <bookmark mark='b'/> Entropy is an average of logs. <bookmark mark='c'/> Swap in the log of the average, <bookmark mark='d'/> and the average of one over p is just the number of outcomes. <bookmark mark='e'/> So H is at most log K, with equality only when every outcome is equally likely. The gap below it is what Shannon called redundancy: structure a guesser can exploit.
8074f9664d62.zh: 一般来说，有K种结果时，熵至多是以2为底K的对数。<bookmark mark='a'/>证明只需要一个不等式。对数函数向下弯，所以对数的平均值，至多等于平均值的对数：詹森不等式。<bookmark mark='b'/>熵是对数的平均值。<bookmark mark='c'/>换成平均值的对数，<bookmark mark='d'/>而p分之1的平均值，正好就是结果的个数。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以H至多是log K，当且仅当每种结果同样可能时取等号。低于它的那段差距，就是香农所说的冗余：猜测者可以利用的结构。

983edfdf8dd4.en: Entropy also works when we know something. Each previous letter gives the next one its own distribution, and entropy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw a column for each previous letter, as wide as that letter is common, as tall as the entropy of what follows. <bookmark mark='b'/> After q, almost nothing: 0.02 bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> After a space, a new word begins: 4.11 bits.
983edfdf8dd4.zh: 当我们知道一些东西时，熵同样适用。每一个前一个字母，都让下一个字母有自己的分布和熵。<bookmark mark='a'/>为每个前一个字母画一根柱子，宽度是这个字母有多常见，高度是它后面那个字母的熵。<bookmark mark='b'/>在q之后，几乎为零：0.02比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>在空格之后，一个新词开始了：4.11比特。

222677086435.en: The total area is the conditional entropy: 3.33 bits given the previous letter, <bookmark mark='a'/> down from 4.08 with no context. <bookmark mark='b'/> On average, knowing more never makes you more uncertain; chapter seven proves it.
222677086435.zh: 总面积就是条件熵：已知前一个字母时是3.33比特，<bookmark mark='a'/>而没有上下文时是4.08比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>平均来说，知道得更多，永远不会让你更不确定；第7章会证明这一点。

72725c72465b.en: Chapter four. Surprise is measured in bits. So let's spend some bits.
72725c72465b.zh: 第4章。意外度用比特来衡量。那我们就来花一些比特。

c3f571a962e7.en: The simplest way to send letters as bits is a fixed-length code. Two to the five is thirty-two, enough for twenty-seven symbols, <bookmark mark='a'/> so each gets a five-bit number. <bookmark mark='b'/> The falcon, 10 symbols, costs 50 bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> But that's wasteful: e is 192 times more common than z, and both cost five bits.
c3f571a962e7.zh: 把字母变成比特，最简单的办法是定长编码。2的5次方是32，足够容纳27个符号，<bookmark mark='a'/>所以每个符号得到一个5位的数。<bookmark mark='b'/>“the falcon”，10个符号，要花50比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>但这很浪费：e比z常见192倍，两者却都要花5比特。

571b2be062c8.en: So give common symbols short codewords, as Morse code gives e a single dot. But careful. <bookmark mark='a'/> If e is zero, t is one, and a is zero one, then zero one could be e, t, or a. <bookmark mark='b'/> The fix is a prefix-free code: no codeword starts another. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the codewords are the leaves of a binary tree: zero goes left, one goes right, and to decode, you walk down from the top to a leaf.
571b2be062c8.zh: 所以给常见的符号短码字，就像摩尔斯电码给e一个点。但要小心。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果e是0，t是1，a是01，那么01可能是e加t，也可能是a。<bookmark mark='b'/>解决办法是无前缀码：没有哪个码字是另一个码字的开头。<bookmark mark='c'/>这样，码字就是一棵二叉树的叶子：0往左，1往右，解码时从顶上往下走，走到叶子为止。

bbaae5114389.en: Watch it decode. Right, right, left: c. Back to the top. Left: a. Right, left: b. Right five times: f. No separators needed.
bbaae5114389.zh: 看它怎么解码。向右、向右、向左：c。回到顶端。向左：a。向右、再向左：b。连续向右五次：f。完全不需要任何分隔符。

915bf940b344.en: Prefix-free codes obey a budget, and the tree shows why. <bookmark mark='a'/> Grow the tree down to the longest codeword: 5 levels, 32 leaves at the bottom. <bookmark mark='b'/> A codeword of length l sits l levels down, and everything below it is off limits, so it uses up two to the l max minus l of the bottom leaves. <bookmark mark='c'/> No codeword starts another, so these shares never overlap: together, at most 32. <bookmark mark='d'/> Divide by two to the l max: two to the minus length, summed over the codewords, is at most one. That's Kraft's inequality, from Leon Kraft's 1949 master's thesis.
915bf940b344.zh: 无前缀码要遵守一个预算，这棵树说明了原因。<bookmark mark='a'/>把树一直长到最长码字的深度：5层，底部有32片叶子。<bookmark mark='b'/>长度为l的码字位于第l层，它下面的一切都不能再用了，所以它占掉了底部2的l max减l次方片叶子。<bookmark mark='c'/>没有哪个码字是另一个的开头，所以这些份额从不重叠：加起来至多32片。<bookmark mark='d'/>除以2的l max次方：对所有码字，2的负码长次方之和至多是1。这就是克拉夫特不等式，出自莱昂·克拉夫特1949年的硕士论文。

7bcf06b1dc86.en: The budget is also enough. <bookmark mark='a'/> Hand me any lengths whose powers of a half add up to at most one, and a prefix code with those lengths exists: give out codewords shortest first, each at the leftmost free node of its depth. <bookmark mark='b'/> For example, round each letter's surprise up to whole bits. The powers of a half add up to 0.70, so here is a prefix code with those lengths. We'll meet it again next chapter.
7bcf06b1dc86.zh: 这个预算也是够用的。<bookmark mark='a'/>给我任何一组码长，只要二分之一的这些次方加起来至多是1，就一定存在恰好有这些码长的前缀码：码字从短到长依次分配，每个都取它那一层里最左边、还空着的节点。<bookmark mark='b'/>举个例子，把每个字母的意外度向上取整成整数比特。二分之一的这些次方加起来是0.70，所以这就是一个有这些码长的前缀码。下一章我们还会再见到它。

e68320d4b726.en: Could a code that isn't prefix-free do better? <bookmark mark='a'/> This one isn't: zero starts zero one. Yet it decodes, because every codeword begins with a zero, and a zero always means a new codeword. Its sum is 15 over 16. <bookmark mark='b'/> This one, with sum 5 over 4, can't be decoded: zero one is a b, or c. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1956 Brockway McMillan showed the budget binds every decodable code. Raise the sum to a power k and multiply out: each term is a message of k codewords. <bookmark mark='d'/> Group the messages by their length in bits. <bookmark mark='e'/> If the code decodes, different messages never give the same bits, so at most two to the m are m bits long, and the sum is at most k times the longest length.
e68320d4b726.zh: 一个不是无前缀的码，能不能做得更好？<bookmark mark='a'/>这个就不是无前缀的：0是01的开头。可它照样能解码，因为每个码字都以0开头，而一个0总是意味着一个新码字。它的和是16分之15。<bookmark mark='b'/>这一个，和是4分之5，就没法解码：01可以是a加b，也可以是c。<bookmark mark='c'/>1956年，布罗克韦·麦克米兰证明，这个预算约束着每一个能解码的码。把这个和取k次方，再乘开：每一项都是一条由k个码字组成的消息。<bookmark mark='d'/>按消息的比特长度把它们分组。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果这个码能解码，不同的消息永远不会给出同样的比特，所以长度为m比特的消息至多有2的m次方条，整个和至多是k乘以最长码长。

210d3e32088a.en: A sum above one, raised to the k, grows exponentially; k times a constant grows in a straight line. <bookmark mark='a'/> For the bad code, five fourths to the k overtakes two k at k equals 16: the bound breaks, so it can't be decodable. <bookmark mark='b'/> So prefix codes lose nothing: any lengths a decodable code can have, a prefix code can have too.
210d3e32088a.zh: 一个大于1的数，取k次方，是指数增长的；而k乘以一个常数，只是沿直线增长。<bookmark mark='a'/>对这个坏的码，四分之五的k次方在k等于16时超过了2k：上界被打破了，所以它不可能是可解码的。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以前缀码什么也不会损失：一个可解码的码能有的码长，前缀码也都能有。

0a1bc7503fcd.en: Chapter five. The best code, and the proof that it is the best.
0a1bc7503fcd.zh: 第5章。最好的编码，以及它为什么是最好的证明。

1567260351c8.en: Now we can prove a speed limit. Let L be the average codeword length, and H the entropy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Write their difference as one sum. <bookmark mark='b'/> Jensen's inequality, exactly as in chapter three, moves the log outside. <bookmark mark='c'/> The probabilities cancel, <bookmark mark='d'/> and Kraft's inequality says what's left is at most log one: zero. <bookmark mark='e'/> So the average length is never less than the entropy, and equals it only if each symbol gets exactly log one over p bits: its surprise.
1567260351c8.zh: 现在可以证明一个速度极限了。设L是平均码长，H是熵。<bookmark mark='a'/>把两者之差写成一个和。<bookmark mark='b'/>詹森不等式，和第3章完全一样，把对数移到外面。<bookmark mark='c'/>概率约掉了，<bookmark mark='d'/>克拉夫特不等式说，剩下的至多是log 1，也就是0。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以平均码长永远不小于熵，只有当每个符号恰好分到p分之1的对数那么多比特，也就是它的意外度时，两者才相等。

3dfa699ce78c.en: Codeword lengths must be whole numbers, so round the surprises up: those lengths fit Kraft's budget, and cost less than one extra bit per symbol. For our letters, 4.62 bits.
3dfa699ce78c.zh: 码长必须是整数，所以把意外度向上取整：这些码长符合克拉夫特的预算，每个符号多花的不到1比特。对我们的字母，是4.62比特。

954091dd317a.en: Which code gets closest? In 1951 David Huffman, a graduate student in Robert Fano's class at MIT, could sit the final exam, or write a paper on finding the most efficient code. He chose the paper. <bookmark mark='a'/> His answer: join the two least likely symbols, here z and q, under a new node whose probability is their sum. Then again with the two least likely of what's left, <bookmark mark='b'/> 26 times, until one tree holds everything.
954091dd317a.zh: 哪种编码最接近？1951年，麻省理工学院的研究生大卫·霍夫曼，在罗伯特·法诺的课上可以选择：参加期末考试，或者写一篇论文，找出最有效的编码。他选了论文。<bookmark mark='a'/>他的答案是：把两个最不可能的符号，这里是z和q，并到一个新节点下，新节点的概率是两者之和。然后对剩下的再取两个最不可能的，再合并，<bookmark mark='b'/>合并26次，直到一棵树装下所有符号。

ae7d800cead0.en: Read off the codewords: <bookmark mark='a'/> the space gets 2 bits, e gets 4, and z gets 10. <bookmark mark='b'/> On average, 4.127 bits per symbol, just 0.043 above the entropy. The falcon now costs 43 bits instead of 50.
ae7d800cead0.zh: 读出码字：<bookmark mark='a'/>空格得到2比特，e得到4，z得到10。<bookmark mark='b'/>平均每个符号4.127比特，只比熵多0.043。“the falcon”现在只要43比特，而不是50。

11dd8f8533fd.en: Huffman proved that no prefix code does better, with a few exchanges. <bookmark mark='a'/> First: if a likelier symbol had a longer codeword than a rarer one, swapping them would shorten the average. Give e the 10 bits of z, and z the 4 bits of e, and each letter costs 0.60 bits more. So in a best code, likelier symbols never get longer codewords. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second: a deepest codeword with no sibling could move up a level. So the deepest codewords come in pairs. <bookmark mark='c'/> By the first exchange, the two rarest symbols can be such a pair: in Huffman's code, z and q, differing only in the last bit.
11dd8f8533fd.zh: 霍夫曼用几次交换证明了，没有哪个前缀码能做得更好。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一：如果一个更可能的符号，码字反而比一个更罕见的长，把两者对调，平均码长就会变短。把z的10比特给e，把e的4比特给z，每个字母平均要多花0.60比特。所以在最好的编码里，更可能的符号，码字绝不会更长。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二：一个最深的码字如果没有兄弟，可以上移一层。所以最深的码字总是成对出现。<bookmark mark='c'/>再由第一次交换，两个最罕见的符号可以就是这样一对：在霍夫曼编码里，是z和q，只有最后一位不同。

f5f548fb04f8.en: Now merge those two rarest symbols into one, whose probability is their sum. <bookmark mark='a'/> Any code for the smaller alphabet becomes one for the original by splitting that leaf, and the average goes up by exactly the merged probability, whatever the rest. So the best code for the original is the best for the smaller problem, plus that split. <bookmark mark='b'/> That's Huffman's first merge, and the same argument covers every merge after it: his tree is optimal. <bookmark mark='c'/> We checked. Add up the weights of the merges: 4.127, Huffman's average. Search every possible shape of code tree for the letters: the best is the same. And on 400 random alphabets, Huffman's code matched the exhaustive search every time.
f5f548fb04f8.zh: 现在把这两个最罕见的符号合并成一个，它的概率是两者之和。<bookmark mark='a'/>小字母表的任何一个编码，只要把那片叶子一分为二，就变成原字母表的编码，而平均码长恰好增加合并后的那个概率，不管其余部分是什么样。所以原问题的最好编码，就是这个更小问题的最好编码，再加上这一分。<bookmark mark='b'/>这就是霍夫曼的第一次合并，同样的论证也适用于之后的每一次合并：他搭出的树是最优的。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们检验过。把每次合并的权重加起来：4.127，正是霍夫曼的平均码长。对这些字母，穷举每一种可能的码树形状：最好的结果是同一个数。在400个随机字母表上，霍夫曼编码每一次都和穷举搜索的结果一致。

bee1ed6c09fc.en: Chapter six. Why long messages compress so well.
bee1ed6c09fc.zh: 第6章。为什么长消息压缩得这么好。

2dd10a4e7247.en: Last chapter, whole bits wasted up to one per symbol, and long blocks were the cure. Here is why. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw letters independently, with the books' frequencies, crude but exact to reason about, and measure the surprise per letter. <bookmark mark='b'/> For one letter, it's all over the place, from 2.4 bits to 10.9. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ten letters: the spread narrows. <bookmark mark='d'/> A hundred, a thousand, ten thousand: it piles up at 4.08 bits, the entropy, its spread shrinking from 1.2 bits to 0.01.
2dd10a4e7247.zh: 上一章里，整数比特让每个符号最多浪费1比特，而长分组是解药。原因在这里。<bookmark mark='a'/>按书里的频率，彼此独立地抽字母，很粗糙，但能精确地推理，然后量一量每个字母的意外度。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有一个字母时，什么值都有，从2.4比特到10.9比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>十个字母：分布收窄了。<bookmark mark='d'/>一百个，一千个，一万个：它堆积到4.08比特，也就是熵，散布从1.2比特缩小到0.01。

12d69afe58d2.en: It's the law of large numbers: a text's surprise is a sum over its letters, and the average of many independent surprises settles at their mean, the entropy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Shannon proved it in 1948; McMillan and Breiman extended it to sources with memory, like real text. Its name: the asymptotic equipartition property.
12d69afe58d2.zh: 这就是大数定律：一段文本的意外度，是它各个字母意外度之和，而许多独立意外度的平均值，会稳定在它们的均值上，也就是熵。<bookmark mark='a'/>香农在1948年证明了它，麦克米兰和布雷曼又把它推广到有记忆的信源，比如真实的文本。它的名字是：渐近均分性。

e11325794c39.en: Call a sequence typical if its surprise per symbol is within a small epsilon of the entropy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Then each has probability close to two to the minus n H. <bookmark mark='b'/> By equipartition, together they hold nearly all the probability. <bookmark mark='c'/> Count them: their probabilities can't add past one, <bookmark mark='d'/> so there are at most two to the n H plus epsilon; <bookmark mark='e'/> and since they hold nearly everything, at least about two to the n H. Almost every sequence you'll see is one of these, all about equally likely.
e11325794c39.zh: 如果一个序列每个符号的意外度，离熵不超过一个小小的ε，就称它是典型的。<bookmark mark='a'/>于是每一个的概率都接近2的负nH次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>由渐近均分性，它们合起来几乎占据了全部概率。<bookmark mark='c'/>数一数它们：它们的概率加起来不能超过1，<bookmark mark='d'/>所以它们至多有2的n乘以H加ε次方个；<bookmark mark='e'/>又因为它们几乎占了一切，所以至少大约有2的nH次方个。你会见到的几乎每一个序列，都是其中之一，它们的可能性都差不多。

8aec77cbefb9.en: Here is the typical set, drawn. Take a simpler source: a coin that writes a space with the books' frequency, 0.191. <bookmark mark='a'/> Lay out all two to the n sequences in a row, equally wide, from the most likely, with no spaces, to the least. <bookmark mark='b'/> Below, the same sequences, each as wide as its probability; the typical ones in gold. <bookmark mark='c'/> With 4 symbols, they are 25 percent of the sequences, holding 40 percent of the probability. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now make the sequences longer.
8aec77cbefb9.zh: 这是把典型集画出来的样子。拿一个更简单的信源：一枚硬币，按书里空格的频率0.191写下一个空格。<bookmark mark='a'/>把所有2的n次方个序列排成一行，一样宽，从最可能的、一个空格都没有的，排到最不可能的。<bookmark mark='b'/>下面是同样这些序列，每个的宽度等于它的概率；典型的涂成金色。<bookmark mark='c'/>n等于4时，它们是全部序列的25%，占了40%的概率。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在让序列变长。

d466b135eb7d.en: In the top row, the gold shrinks to a sliver, then to nothing you can see; in the bottom row it spreads until it fills almost everything. <bookmark mark='a'/> By 1000 symbols, the typical sequences are two to the minus 173 of all sequences, and carry all but one part in 87 million of the probability. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the most likely sequence, all non-spaces, isn't typical at all: you'll essentially never see it.
d466b135eb7d.zh: 在上面一行，金色缩成一条细缝，然后细到看不见；在下面一行，它不断扩展，直到几乎填满一切。<bookmark mark='a'/>到1000个符号时，典型序列只占全部序列的2的负173次方，却占了全部概率，只差87百万分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>而那个最可能的序列，一个空格都没有，根本不是典型的：你几乎永远不会见到它。

d2aebdf9ab79.en: That gives the source coding theorem. <bookmark mark='a'/> To compress n symbols: if the sequence is typical, send a zero, then its number in a list of the typical set: about n H bits. If not, send a one and the sequence itself. That's rare, so on average you pay about H bits per symbol. <bookmark mark='b'/> And no code does better: a shorter list would miss most typical sequences, and almost all the probability. <bookmark mark='c'/> Even last chapter's rounded code, used on whole blocks, closes in on the entropy: 0.882 bits per symbol with blocks of 4, 0.7041 with blocks of 1000, against 0.7036.
d2aebdf9ab79.zh: 这就给出了信源编码定理。<bookmark mark='a'/>要压缩n个符号：如果序列是典型的，先发一个0，再发它在典型集清单里的编号：大约nH比特。如果不是，就发一个1，再把序列原样发出去。这种情况很少，所以平均下来，每个符号大约花H比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>而且没有哪个编码能做得更好：更短的清单会漏掉大部分典型序列，也就漏掉了几乎全部概率。<bookmark mark='c'/>就连上一章的取整编码，用在整个分组上，也会逼近熵：分组长4时每个符号0.882比特，分组长1000时是0.7041，而熵是0.7036。

1716cb109987.en: Now English: twenty-seven to the n strings of n letters. <bookmark mark='a'/> Under letter frequencies alone, the typical ones are a fraction two to the minus 0.67 n: for a page of 2,000 letters, two to the minus 1,341. <bookmark mark='b'/> At one bit per letter, real text is a far smaller corner. <bookmark mark='c'/> A language model's job is to find that corner, and to write, it draws from it: how, in Part 5.
1716cb109987.zh: 现在来看英语：n个字母的字符串有27的n次方个。<bookmark mark='a'/>只按字母频率，典型的字符串也只占其中2的负0.67n次方：对一页2000个字母，是2的负1341次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>按每个字母1比特，真实的文本是一个小得多的角落。<bookmark mark='c'/>语言模型的工作，就是找到这个角落；要写东西时，就从里面抽取：怎么抽，在第5部分。

7c25637abef7.en: Chapter seven. What happens when your guesses are wrong?
7c25637abef7.zh: 第7章。如果你的猜测错了，会怎样？

5ea42f84345c.en: Codes and guesses are the same thing: a code that spends l bits on a symbol bets that it has probability two to the minus l. What if the bets are wrong? <bookmark mark='a'/> Say the data come from p, but the code was built for a model q. Each symbol costs log of one over q bits, and on average we pay the cross-entropy: the sum of p times log one over q.
5ea42f84345c.zh: 编码和猜测是同一回事：一个在某个符号上花l比特的编码，等于是在赌这个符号的概率是2的负l次方。那如果赌错了呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>假设数据来自p，编码却是为模型q设计的。每个符号要花q分之1的对数那么多比特，平均下来，我们付出的是交叉熵：p乘以q分之1的对数，再求和。

571da0da5add.en: As a picture: <bookmark mark='a'/> with the right probabilities, the area is the entropy, 4.08 bits. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now use a model that has e and z the wrong way round. Every e, one symbol in 10, now costs 10.9 bits. The area grows to 4.84.
571da0da5add.zh: 画成一幅图：<bookmark mark='a'/>用正确的概率，面积就是熵，4.08比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在用一个把e和z弄反了的模型。每个e，大约每10个符号就有一个，现在要花10.9比特。面积增大到4.84。

ef823cc7bc72.en: Split the log in two, <bookmark mark='a'/> and the cross-entropy separates into two prices. First, the entropy of p: the world's own randomness, which no code can remove. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second, the price of being wrong: the Kullback–Leibler divergence of q from p, from 1951. <bookmark mark='c'/> Swapping e and z costs 0.75 bits per symbol. The letter frequencies of our thirty books, used on the Falcon passage, are wrong by less than a hundredth of a bit.
ef823cc7bc72.zh: 把对数拆成两部分，<bookmark mark='a'/>交叉熵就分成了两笔代价。第一笔是p的熵：世界本身的随机性，任何编码都消除不了。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二笔是犯错的代价：q相对于p的库尔巴克–莱布勒散度，1951年提出。<bookmark mark='c'/>把e和z对调，每个符号多花0.75比特。我们30本书的字母频率，用在《马耳他之鹰》的段落上，错得不到百分之一比特。

13cad020c7b3.en: Is being wrong always a cost? Yes, by chapter three's argument. <bookmark mark='a'/> The log bends downward: the average of logs is at most the log of the average. <bookmark mark='b'/> Minus the divergence is an average, weighted by p, of the log of q over p. <bookmark mark='c'/> Move the log outside. <bookmark mark='d'/> Inside, the p's cancel, <bookmark mark='e'/> and what's left is the total of q, which is one. The log of one is zero.
13cad020c7b3.zh: 犯错总是要付出代价吗？是的，用的是第3章的论证。<bookmark mark='a'/>对数向下弯：对数的平均值，至多等于平均值的对数。<bookmark mark='b'/>负的散度，是以p为权重，对q除以p的对数求的平均。<bookmark mark='c'/>把对数移到外面。<bookmark mark='d'/>里面的p约掉了，<bookmark mark='e'/>剩下的是q的总和，也就是1。1的对数是0。

4cce220668d9.en: So the divergence is never negative, and zero only when q equals p, where Jensen's inequality is an equality. <bookmark mark='a'/> The truth is the best code. The inequality is named after Josiah Willard Gibbs, who used it in statistical mechanics. <bookmark mark='b'/> It also pays a debt from chapter three: the drop in entropy from knowing X is a divergence too, so it can't be negative. Knowing more never hurts, on average. <bookmark mark='c'/> That drop, the mutual information, gets its own chapter.
4cce220668d9.zh: 所以散度永远不会是负的，只有当q等于p时才为零，这时詹森不等式取等号。<bookmark mark='a'/>真相就是最好的编码。这个不等式以约西亚·威拉德·吉布斯命名，他在统计力学里用过它。<bookmark mark='b'/>它还还上了第3章欠下的债：知道X之后熵的下降，也是一个散度，所以不可能是负的。平均来说，知道得更多永远没有坏处。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个下降，也就是互信息，会有自己的一章。

7fae89c28a8c.en: Here is why this matters for AI. <bookmark mark='a'/> The loss every large language model is trained to minimize is exactly this: the average of log one over q, for each token of real text, given the tokens before it. <bookmark mark='n'/> Usually with the natural log, ln, so it's counted in nats: one nat is about 1.44 bits. <bookmark mark='b'/> It's the cross-entropy between the world's text and the model. <bookmark mark='c'/> Training can only shrink the divergence; <bookmark mark='d'/> the entropy of language itself is a floor no model can go below.
7fae89c28a8c.zh: 这就是它对AI的意义所在。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一个大语言模型训练时要最小化的损失，正是这个：对真实文本的每一个词元，在已知前面词元的条件下，取q分之1的对数，再求平均。<bookmark mark='n'/>通常用自然对数ln，所以单位是奈特：1奈特大约是1.44比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>它就是世界上的文本和模型之间的交叉熵。<bookmark mark='c'/>训练只能缩小散度；<bookmark mark='d'/>语言本身的熵，是任何模型都无法低于的下限。

9808020e2fb0.en: One more property, which will matter a lot later: the divergence is not symmetric. Say the truth p has two peaks, and our model q can only be a bell curve: one smooth hump, set by its center and its width. Which bell curve is best? It depends on which way round we measure. <bookmark mark='a'/> Minimizing the divergence of q from p, the training loss we just met, <bookmark mark='b'/> pulls q wide, to cover both peaks: it ends with exactly p's mean and spread.
9808020e2fb0.zh: 还有一个性质，后面会非常重要：散度不是对称的。假设真实的p有两个峰，而我们的模型q只能是一条钟形曲线：一个平滑的鼓包，由它的中心和宽度决定。哪条钟形曲线最好？这取决于我们按哪个方向去量。<bookmark mark='a'/>最小化q相对于p的散度，也就是我们刚见过的训练损失，<bookmark mark='b'/>会把q拉宽，盖住两个峰：最后它的均值和散布恰好与p相同。

28feb26b0a98.en: The other way round, <bookmark mark='a'/> q is punished for putting probability where p has none, so it squeezes into a single peak and ignores the other. Each fit is bad by the other's measure: the wide curve scores 1.30 bits the second way, the narrow one 10.1 bits the first. <bookmark mark='b'/> Covering everything, or committing to one thing: that choice comes back in variational autoencoders, in Part 20, and in distillation and reinforcement learning from human feedback, in Part 27.
28feb26b0a98.zh: 反过来，<bookmark mark='a'/>q在p没有概率的地方放了概率，就会受罚，所以它挤进一个峰里，不管另一个。每种拟合，按另一种标准都很糟：宽的那条曲线，按第二种方式量是1.30比特；窄的那条，按第一种方式量是10.1比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>覆盖一切，还是认定一个：这个选择会在第20部分的变分自编码器里再次出现，也会在第27部分的蒸馏和基于人类反馈的强化学习里出现。

353d4e8ebcfb.en: Chapter eight. The best code for a good guesser.
353d4e8ebcfb.zh: 第8章。给好猜测者的最好编码。

0c6e39f7262e.en: Huffman's code has one flaw: every symbol costs at least one whole bit. <bookmark mark='a'/> u after q carries 0.002 bits, and still costs a full bit. <bookmark mark='b'/> A model that really knows English is surprised by about a bit per symbol, or less; a symbol code can't go below one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Long blocks would fix it, but blocks of a hundred letters need a table of twenty-seven to the hundred entries. <bookmark mark='d'/> Instead, code the whole message as one number, one guess at a time.
0c6e39f7262e.zh: 霍夫曼编码有一个缺陷：每个符号至少要花整整1比特。<bookmark mark='a'/>q后面的u只携带0.002比特，却还是要花整整1比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个真正懂英语的模型，每个符号的意外度只有大约1比特，甚至更少；逐符号的编码不能低于1比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>长分组能解决这个问题，可是一百个字母一组，码表就需要27的100次方个条目。<bookmark mark='d'/>换个办法：把整条消息编成一个数，一次一个猜测。

51519f33251d.en: Arithmetic coding, worked out by Jorma Rissanen and Richard Pasco in 1976. We've seen its heart: the nested slivers of the chain rule. <bookmark mark='a'/> Split the unit interval by the model's guesses for the first letter: t takes a sliver 0.155 wide. Write its two ends in binary. <bookmark mark='b'/> They agree on their first 2 digits, so every number in the sliver starts that way: those bits are decided.
51519f33251d.zh: 算术编码，由约尔马·里萨宁和理查德·帕斯科在1976年提出。我们已经见过它的核心：链式法则那一层套一层的小段。<bookmark mark='a'/>按模型对第一个字母的猜测，分割单位区间：t分到一段，宽0.155。把它的两个端点写成二进制。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们的前2位相同，所以这一段里的每个数都这样开头：这几位已经确定了。

bd875fa80ea6.en: Then zoom in and split again: h, e, space, f, a, l, c, o, n. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each letter narrows the interval by its probability, and more leading digits of its ends come to agree, ready to send. <bookmark mark='b'/> A likely letter barely narrows it, and costs a fraction of a bit. An unlikely one, like the c in falcon, which the model gave 0.8 percent, costs 7.0 bits.
bd875fa80ea6.zh: 然后放大，再分割：h、e、空格、f、a、l、c、o、n。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个字母都按它的概率把区间缩小，两个端点相同的前导位越来越多，随时可以发送。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个可能的字母几乎不缩小区间，只花一个零头比特。一个不太可能的字母，比如falcon里的c，模型只给了它0.8%，就要花7.0比特。

c78eaa141666.en: After ten letters, the interval has width two to the minus 27.66: the probability of the whole message. <bookmark mark='a'/> To finish, find the shortest binary fraction whose every continuation lies inside the interval. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here, it takes 29 bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Compare: 50 for the fixed code, 43 for Huffman, 29 for arithmetic coding, against an information content of 27.66.
c78eaa141666.zh: 十个字母之后，区间的宽度是2的负27.66次方：整条消息的概率。<bookmark mark='a'/>最后，找出最短的二进制小数，使它后面无论接什么，都落在区间内。<bookmark mark='b'/>这里需要29比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>比一比：定长编码50比特，霍夫曼43比特，算术编码29比特，而信息量是27.66比特。

db7f7113cc9b.en: Why within two bits? Let P be the message's probability, the width of its interval. <bookmark mark='a'/> Choose a length l: log of one over P, rounded up, plus one. <bookmark mark='b'/> A run of l bits names a little interval of width two to the minus l, at most half of P. <bookmark mark='c'/> These tile the line, so the first one starting at or after the low end finishes before the high end: it lies inside, and its l bits pin the message down. <bookmark mark='d'/> And l is less than the information content plus two.
db7f7113cc9b.zh: 为什么不超过2比特？设P是消息的概率，也就是它的区间宽度。<bookmark mark='a'/>选一个长度l：P分之1的对数，向上取整，再加1。<bookmark mark='b'/>一串l位比特代表一个宽度为2的负l次方的小区间，至多是P的一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些小区间铺满整条线，所以在低端处或之后开始的第一个小区间，一定在高端之前结束：它整个落在里面，它的l位比特就锁定了这条消息。<bookmark mark='d'/>而l小于信息量加2。

30cade03720b.en: Decoding runs the same steps, with an identical copy of the model. <bookmark mark='a'/> The bits name a number. It falls in the t sliver of the first split: the first letter is t. <bookmark mark='b'/> Zoom in: the h sliver, then e, and so on, until the message is back, exactly.
30cade03720b.zh: 解码走的是同样的步骤，用一份完全相同的模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>这些比特代表一个数。它落在第一次分割中t的那一段里：第一个字母是t。<bookmark mark='b'/>放大：h的那一段，然后是e，依此类推，直到消息被原样还原。

a9d049941b66.en: A real coder keeps the interval as two whole numbers, low and high: 16 bits here, 32 in practice. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first letter narrows it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Both ends agree on their leading bit: send it, and double the half holding the interval: a zoom. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the interval straddles the middle, the next bit isn't known yet: the coder zooms about the middle anyway, and the waiting bit comes out, flipped, after the next decided one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Narrow and zoom, and the bits stream out.
a9d049941b66.zh: 真正的编码器把区间存成两个整数，低端和高端：这里是16位，实际中是32位。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一个字母缩小区间。<bookmark mark='b'/>两端的第一位相同了：把它发出去，再把装着区间的那一半放大一倍：这就是一次放大。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果区间跨过中点，下一位还不知道：编码器照样以中点为中心放大，等下一个确定的位出来之后，那个等待中的位会被翻转，跟着出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>缩小，放大，比特就源源不断地流出来。

910c2e065ef2.en: At the end, a couple of bits close it off: 28 bits for the falcon, one fewer than the exact coder's 29. Whole numbers, and nothing longer than the registers, ever.
910c2e065ef2.zh: 最后，再用几位把它收尾：“the falcon”用了28比特，比精确编码器的29比特少1比特。始终是整数，而且从不超过寄存器的长度。

5c12038682fa.en: This is the hinge of the whole part. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give arithmetic coding any model that predicts, and you get a compressor spending about log of one over q bits per symbol: the text's length times the model's cross-entropy. <bookmark mark='b'/> And any compressor defines a model: a text that takes l bits gets probability two to the minus l. <bookmark mark='c'/> Predicting well and compressing well are the same skill. In chapter fifteen, a language model becomes a compressor.
5c12038682fa.zh: 这是整个这一部分的枢纽。<bookmark mark='a'/>把任何一个能预测的模型交给算术编码，就得到一个压缩器，每个符号大约花q分之1的对数那么多比特：文本的长度乘以模型的交叉熵。<bookmark mark='b'/>反过来，任何压缩器都定义了一个模型：一段要花l比特的文本，就被赋予了2的负l次方的概率。<bookmark mark='c'/>预测得好和压缩得好，是同一种本事。在第15章，一个语言模型会变成压缩器。

26d849fedb9a.en: Chapter nine. So far, our models have only counted. How far can counting go?
26d849fedb9a.zh: 第9章。到目前为止，我们的模型只会计数。计数能走多远？

afea873ec2d1.en: In 1948, Shannon let counting models write. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every symbol equally likely: noise. <bookmark mark='b'/> The right letter frequencies: still noise, with the right texture. <bookmark mark='c'/> Pick each letter by what followed the previous one in our books, and syllables appear. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two letters of context: short words. <bookmark mark='e'/> Four: mostly real words. <bookmark mark='f'/> Six: phrases, mariners would be by many. <bookmark mark='g'/> Count whole words instead, and it almost scans.
afea873ec2d1.zh: 1948年，香农让计数模型自己写东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个符号同样可能：噪声。<bookmark mark='b'/>用对的字母频率：还是噪声，但纹理对了。<bookmark mark='c'/>按我们书里前一个字母后面跟什么来选每个字母，音节就出现了。<bookmark mark='d'/>两个字母的上下文：短词。<bookmark mark='e'/>四个：大多是真的词。<bookmark mark='f'/>六个：出现了短语，mariners would be by many。<bookmark mark='g'/>改成数整个的词，读起来几乎有点韵律了。

4d69cba5cbee.en: The rule behind all of these is simple. <bookmark mark='a'/> The probability of the next symbol, given a context, is how often it followed that context in the books, divided by how often the context appeared. <bookmark mark='b'/> It's the most natural estimate, and chapter eleven shows it's the best one, for the books themselves.
4d69cba5cbee.zh: 这些背后的规则很简单。<bookmark mark='a'/>在给定上下文时，下一个符号的概率，等于它在书里跟在这个上下文后面的次数，除以这个上下文出现的次数。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是最自然的估计，第11章会说明，对这些书本身来说，它也是最好的估计。

dcf626c22878.en: So let's score them. For each amount of context, from none to fourteen letters, measure the bits per letter. <bookmark mark='a'/> First on the books it counted. More context, fewer bits, down to 0.27 bits per letter at 14 letters. Our numbers for no context and one letter, 4.08 and 3.33, <bookmark mark='b'/> land next to Shannon's 1951 estimates from printed tables, 4.03 and 3.32.
dcf626c22878.zh: 我们来给它们打分。对每一种上下文长度，从0个字母到14个，量一量每个字母的比特数。<bookmark mark='a'/>先在它数过的那些书上。上下文越多，比特越少，在14个字母时，降到每个字母0.27比特。我们在没有上下文和一个字母上下文时的数字，4.08和3.33，<bookmark mark='b'/>和香农1951年根据印刷的统计表做的估计4.03和3.32很接近。

853eff3b1005.en: But on new text, the Falcon passage, <bookmark mark='a'/> the story is different. More context helps at first: <bookmark mark='b'/> the best is 5 letters of context, at 2.02 bits per letter. Beyond that, it gets worse: with 14 letters of context it's worse than knowing nothing but letter frequencies.
853eff3b1005.zh: 但在新的文本，也就是《马耳他之鹰》的段落上，<bookmark mark='a'/>情况就不同了。上下文一开始有帮助：<bookmark mark='b'/>最好的是5个字母的上下文，每个字母2.02比特。再往后就变差了：用14个字母的上下文时，甚至比只知道字母频率还差。

61021629f44b.en: The reason: contexts multiply. <bookmark mark='a'/> Of the Falcon passage's five-letter contexts, 99 percent appear somewhere in the books; of its 14-letter contexts, only 27 percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> There are about ten to the 20 possible 14-letter contexts, and the books hold 16.7 million. <bookmark mark='c'/> An unseen context gives the model nothing to go on, and a letter never seen after it would get probability zero: infinite surprise.
61021629f44b.zh: 原因是：上下文会成倍增长。<bookmark mark='a'/>《马耳他之鹰》段落里5个字母的上下文，99%在书里的某个地方出现过；它的14个字母的上下文，只有27%出现过。<bookmark mark='b'/>可能的14个字母的上下文大约有10的20次方个，而书里只有16.7百万个。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个没见过的上下文，模型毫无依据；在它后面从没见过的字母，概率会是零：意外度无穷大。

199ef6ff59dd.en: The patch is older than computers. In 1814 Pierre-Simon Laplace asked: if something happened s times in n tries, how likely is it next time? <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose that, before looking, every chance between zero and one was equally plausible. Weigh each by how well it explains what you saw, <bookmark mark='b'/> and the answer is s plus one, over n plus two. <bookmark mark='c'/> His example was the sunrise: five thousand years, 1,826,213 days, give odds of 1,826,214 to one that the sun rises tomorrow. <bookmark mark='d'/> For our 27 symbols: add one to every count, and nothing gets probability zero. <bookmark mark='e'/> Add alpha instead of one, chosen on held-out text, and you have the smoothing that keeps our curves finite.
199ef6ff59dd.zh: 这个补救办法比计算机还要古老。1814年，皮埃尔–西蒙·拉普拉斯问：如果一件事在n次尝试中发生了s次，下一次它发生的可能性有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>假设在观察之前，0到1之间的每一个机会都同样可信。按每个机会对你所见的解释程度给它加权，<bookmark mark='b'/>答案就是s加1，除以n加2。<bookmark mark='c'/>他的例子是日出：五千年，1826213天，得出明天太阳升起的赔率是1826214比1。<bookmark mark='d'/>对我们的27个符号：给每个计数加1，就没有哪个会得到零概率。<bookmark mark='e'/>把加1换成加α，α在留出的文本上选定，就是让我们的曲线保持有限的那种平滑。

493d0bc9af1e.en: How much does alpha matter? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is every alpha from a ten-thousandth to ten, at four context lengths, on the Falcon passage. <bookmark mark='b'/> For one letter of context, Laplace's rule is as good as anything: its contexts are seen millions of times. <bookmark mark='c'/> With 8 letters of context, 23 percent of the passage's letters follow a context where the books never showed that letter, and most contexts were seen only a few times. Adding one to every count drowns the evidence: Laplace's rule costs 0.35 bits per letter more than the alpha chosen on held-out text, 0.04. Good smoothing is about what you haven't seen; Part 7 answers it properly.
493d0bc9af1e.zh: α有多重要？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是从万分之一到10的每一个α，在四种上下文长度下，在《马耳他之鹰》段落上的得分。<bookmark mark='b'/>对一个字母的上下文，拉普拉斯法则不比任何别的差：它的上下文都见过几百万次。<bookmark mark='c'/>用8个字母的上下文时，段落里23%的字母，跟在一个书里从没在它后面出现过这个字母的上下文之后，而大多数上下文只见过寥寥几次。给每个计数加1，就淹没了证据：拉普拉斯法则每个字母比在留出文本上选出的α，也就是0.04，多花0.35比特。好的平滑，关乎你没见过的东西；第7部分会好好地回答它。

74daa0d318a6.en: This is the first appearance of the central problem of machine learning. <bookmark mark='a'/> A model can fit the data it learned from almost perfectly, and still guess badly on new data; how well it does there is called generalization. <bookmark mark='b'/> Counting has a deeper limit: every context is an island. It can't tell that the dog barked and the hound barked are alike, so it can't share what it learned. <bookmark mark='c'/> Better smoothing comes in Part 7, generalization in Part 8, and models that share what they learn, with vectors and networks, in Parts 3 and 9.
74daa0d318a6.zh: 这是机器学习核心问题的第一次登场。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个模型可以几乎完美地拟合它学过的数据，却仍然在新数据上猜得很差；它在新数据上做得怎么样，叫作泛化。<bookmark mark='b'/>计数还有一个更深的局限：每个上下文都是一座孤岛。它分不清the dog barked和the hound barked是相似的，所以没法分享它学到的东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>更好的平滑在第7部分，泛化在第8部分，而能分享所学的模型，靠的是向量和网络，在第3部分和第9部分。

3c7b1155c8ae.en: Chapter ten. Back to Shannon's guessing game, now that we have the tools to read it.
3c7b1155c8ae.zh: 第10章。回到香农的猜字游戏，现在我们有了读懂它的工具。

6552b5f71461.en: Here's Shannon's key observation. Give the receiver an identical twin of the guesser: same knowledge, same habits. <bookmark mark='a'/> The sender plays the game on the text and sends only the guess counts. <bookmark mark='b'/> The receiver asks the twin, and when the count says third guess, takes its third guess. Out comes the text, exactly.
6552b5f71461.zh: 这是香农的关键洞见。给接收方一个和猜测者一模一样的双胞胎：同样的知识，同样的习惯。<bookmark mark='a'/>发送方在文本上玩猜字游戏，只把猜测次数发出去。<bookmark mark='b'/>接收方去问双胞胎，次数说第三次，就取它的第三次猜测。文本就原样出来了。

80e6bf4d7d27.en: So the guess counts carry all the text's information. <bookmark mark='a'/> The text's entropy is at most theirs, which is at most the entropy of how often each guess number turns up: an upper bound on the information in English.
80e6bf4d7d27.zh: 所以猜测次数携带了文本的全部信息。<bookmark mark='a'/>文本的熵至多等于猜测次数的熵，而后者又至多等于各个猜测次数出现频率的熵：这就是英语信息量的一个上界。

78375e8e0c70.en: Let's play with the last chapter's counting model as the guesser, on 11,994 letters of the Falcon passage. <bookmark mark='a'/> It gets the letter first time 58 percent of the time, second time 13 percent, with a long tail.
78375e8e0c70.zh: 我们让上一章的计数模型当猜测者，在《马耳他之鹰》段落的11994个字母上玩这个游戏。<bookmark mark='a'/>它第一次就猜中的情况占58%，第二次猜中的占13%，后面还拖着一条长尾巴。

88378ac78ec8.en: Later estimates, with people betting on the next letter, landed at about 1.3 bits. <bookmark mark='a'/> To guess like a person, a machine has to know what a person knows.
88378ac78ec8.zh: 后来的估计，让人对下一个字母下注，结果落在每个字母大约1.3比特。<bookmark mark='a'/>要像人一样猜，机器就得知道人所知道的东西。

31f7c0106e61.en: Chapter eleven. So far our models were counted. Now let's see how a model learns.
31f7c0106e61.zh: 第11章。到目前为止，我们的模型都是数出来的。现在来看一个模型怎样学习。

942a603d807c.en: Learning starts from a principle stated by Ronald Fisher in 1922: choose the model under which the data you saw were most likely. The likelihood is the product of the model's probabilities for every observation. <bookmark mark='a'/> Minus its log, per observation, is the average surprise. <bookmark mark='b'/> Group the observations by value: the cross-entropy between the data's own frequencies, p hat, and the model. <bookmark mark='c'/> That's the data's entropy plus the model's divergence from the data.
942a603d807c.zh: 学习始于罗纳德·费希尔在1922年提出的一个原则：选择那个让你看到的数据最有可能出现的模型。似然，就是模型给每一个观测的概率的乘积。<bookmark mark='a'/>对它取负对数，再除以观测数，就是平均意外度。<bookmark mark='b'/>把观测按取值归类：这就是数据自身的频率p帽与模型之间的交叉熵。<bookmark mark='c'/>它等于数据的熵，加上模型相对于数据的散度。

7cb4293bab0b.en: So maximum likelihood, minimum cross-entropy, and minimum divergence from the data are one and the same goal. It's the loss from chapter seven, seen from the other side.
7cb4293bab0b.zh: 所以最大似然、最小交叉熵、与数据的最小散度，是同一个目标。这就是第7章的损失，从另一边看过去。

2a178a2e294c.en: If the model may be any distribution at all, <bookmark mark='a'/> the divergence is smallest, zero, when the model equals the data's frequencies. <bookmark mark='b'/> So chapter nine's counting models were maximum likelihood models, and that's why they overfit: they fit the books perfectly, and nothing pulled them toward anything more general.
2a178a2e294c.zh: 如果模型可以是任何一个分布，<bookmark mark='a'/>当模型等于数据自身的频率时，散度最小，为零。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以第9章的计数模型就是最大似然模型，这也正是它们过拟合的原因：它们完美地拟合了那些书，却没有任何东西把它们拉向更一般的东西。

e6ec375af070.en: Counting doesn't generalize. Neural networks do. <bookmark mark='n'/> A neural network is a stack of simple steps: multiply by a table of numbers, bend the result, repeat, with all the numbers tuned until its guesses are good. For each possible next token, its last step computes a score, a logit: <bookmark mark='a'/> any real number, positive or negative. <bookmark mark='b'/> To make probabilities, exponentiate: e to the z is always positive, and each step of one up multiplies it by about 2.7. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then divide by the total. That's the softmax: bigger score, bigger probability, and never zero.
e6ec375af070.zh: 计数不会泛化。神经网络会。<bookmark mark='n'/>神经网络是一叠简单的步骤：乘以一张数表，把结果弯一弯，然后重复；所有的数都要不断调整，直到它猜得好为止。对每一个可能的下一个词元，它的最后一步会算出一个分数，叫作logit：<bookmark mark='a'/>任意实数，可正可负。<bookmark mark='b'/>要变成概率，先取指数：e的z次方总是正的，z每增加1，它就大约乘以2.7。<bookmark mark='c'/>再除以总和。这就是softmax：分数越高，概率越大，而且永远不会是零。

3c6bfba32dfb.en: To learn, the network needs to know which way to nudge each score. <bookmark mark='n'/> That's what a derivative measures: how much the output moves when you nudge one input, holding the others still. <bookmark mark='a'/> Write the surprise of the right answer, y, in terms of the scores. <bookmark mark='b'/> Differentiate with respect to the score z k. The first term gives minus one if k is y. The second is the softmax itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the derivative is q k minus one, for the right answer, and q k, for every wrong one.
3c6bfba32dfb.zh: 要学习，网络需要知道每个分数该往哪边推。<bookmark mark='n'/>这正是导数衡量的东西：把一个输入推一点点，其他输入保持不动，输出会变化多少。<bookmark mark='a'/>用这些分数写出正确答案y的意外度。<bookmark mark='b'/>对分数z k求导。第一项在k等于y时给出负1。第二项就是softmax本身。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以导数是：对正确答案，q k减1；对每个错误答案，就是q k。

90335d365ced.en: In words: the model's guess, minus the truth. <bookmark mark='a'/> Averaged over a dataset, the gradient is q minus p hat. Push up the scores of what happened more often than the model expected; push down the rest. Every language model, however large, ends in exactly this step. <bookmark mark='b'/> Following it downhill, one small step at a time, is gradient descent, and it returns in Parts 4, 9 and 11.
90335d365ced.zh: 用一句话说：模型的猜测，减去真相。<bookmark mark='a'/>在整个数据集上平均，梯度就是q减去p帽。比模型预期出现得更多的，把它的分数往上推；其余的往下推。每一个语言模型，不管多大，最后一步都正是这样。<bookmark mark='b'/>沿着它一小步一小步地往下坡走，就是梯度下降，它会在第4、9和11部分再次出现。

c89cfa992c15.en: Chapter twelve. What the past tells you about the future.
c89cfa992c15.zh: 第12章。过去告诉了你多少关于未来的事。

9447b2ece19f.en: In chapter seven, knowing X lowered the entropy of Y, on average. That drop is the mutual information. <bookmark mark='a'/> It's the bits that knowing one thing saves you when you guess the other, and it's symmetric. It's also a divergence, of the joint distribution from independence, so it's never negative. <bookmark mark='b'/> In our books, the next letter carries 4.08 bits; knowing the letter before it, 3.33. <bookmark mark='c'/> So neighbouring letters share 0.75 bits. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two letters back share 1.36, though the second one on its own shares only 0.27: together, letters say more than apart.
9447b2ece19f.zh: 在第7章，知道X之后，Y的熵平均会下降。这个下降就是互信息。<bookmark mark='a'/>它是你知道一件事之后，猜另一件事时能省下的比特数，而且它是对称的。它也是一个散度，是联合分布相对于两者独立时的散度，所以永远不会是负的。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们的书里，下一个字母携带4.08比特；知道它前面那个字母时，是3.33比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以相邻的字母共享0.75比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>往前两个字母，共享1.36比特，而第二个字母单独只共享0.27：字母合在一起，说的比分开时多。

4b2eed15c074.en: Now process what you know. Suppose Z is computed from Y, by any function at all, even a noisy one. <bookmark mark='a'/> The chain rule splits what Y and Z together say about X in two ways: first Y, then whatever Z adds, which is nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Or first Z, then whatever Y adds. <bookmark mark='c'/> Compare the two, and Z can never tell you more about X than Y did. No amount of processing creates information.
4b2eed15c074.zh: 现在来处理你知道的东西。假设Z是由Y算出来的，用什么函数都行，哪怕是带噪声的。<bookmark mark='a'/>链式法则可以用两种方式拆开Y和Z合起来告诉你的关于X的东西：先是Y，再加上Z额外带来的，而那是零。<bookmark mark='b'/>或者先是Z，再加上Y额外带来的。<bookmark mark='c'/>比较这两种拆法，Z告诉你的关于X的，永远不会比Y多。再怎么处理，也创造不出信息。

87374d059feb.en: Let's watch it happen in our books. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep only the kind of the previous letter: space, vowel or consonant. Of the 0.75 bits, 0.35 survive. <bookmark mark='b'/> Or garble it: replace a share of the letters with random ones. The more noise, the less it tells, down to nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> Do both, and you lose more: each curve stays under the one before. <bookmark mark='d'/> A law for learning machines too: whatever a network computes from its context can't know more about the next token than the context itself.
87374d059feb.zh: 我们在书里看看它是怎么发生的。<bookmark mark='a'/>只保留前一个字母的类别：空格、元音还是辅音。0.75比特里，留下了0.35比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>或者把它弄乱：把一部分字母换成随机的字母。噪声越多，它告诉你的就越少，一直降到零。<bookmark mark='c'/>两样都做，损失更多：每一条曲线都待在前一条的下面。<bookmark mark='d'/>这对学习机器也是一条定律：一个网络无论从它的上下文里算出什么，对下一个词元的了解，都不会超过上下文本身。

2e20fdcc09e7.en: How far back does that reach? Measure the mutual information between a letter and the one d places later, over all our books. <bookmark mark='a'/> Neighbours share 0.75 bits. Inside a word, it falls fast. <bookmark mark='b'/> But then it doesn't vanish. It decays slowly, like a power of the distance, out to a thousand letters and beyond. On these axes, each tick is ten times the last, both across and up, so a power law shows up as a straight line.
2e20fdcc09e7.zh: 这能回溯多远？量一量一个字母和d个位置之后那个字母之间的互信息，用上我们所有的书。<bookmark mark='a'/>相邻的字母共享0.75比特。在一个词里面，它下降得很快。<bookmark mark='b'/>但它并没有消失。它衰减得很慢，像距离的幂次一样，一直到一千个字母以外。在这些坐标轴上，每个刻度都是前一个的10倍，横轴纵轴都是，所以幂律显示为一条直线。

aebe9e4df7db.en: A counting model can't produce that tail: beyond its few letters of context, its dependence dies away exponentially, <bookmark mark='x'/> by the same factor every letter, straight off these axes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Real text rewards memory at every distance. To guess well, a model needs a long memory, and a way to find what matters in it: attention, in Part 13.
aebe9e4df7db.zh: 计数模型产生不了这样的尾巴：超出它那几个字母的上下文，依赖关系就按指数消失，<bookmark mark='x'/>每多一个字母就缩小同样的倍数，直直地掉出这些坐标轴。<bookmark mark='a'/>真实的文本，在每一个距离上都奖励记忆。要猜得好，模型需要长的记忆，还需要一种办法，找出其中要紧的部分：注意力，在第13部分。

45d4c60150b8.en: Chapter thirteen. What does a model have to know, to guess well?
45d4c60150b8.zh: 第13章。要猜得好，模型需要知道什么？

381d5f6b6425.en: Let's look at what a strong model knows that a weaker one doesn't. Here is a paragraph of the Falcon passage, in tokens, <bookmark mark='a'/> each colored by how surprised GPT-2, from 2019, was by it: dark when expected, bright when not. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the same paragraph under Qwen3, from 2025. Its tiles are darker almost everywhere: 350 bits instead of 446.
381d5f6b6425.zh: 我们来看看，一个强的模型知道什么，而弱的模型不知道。这是《马耳他之鹰》段落里的一段，切成了词元，<bookmark mark='a'/>每个都按2019年的GPT-2对它有多意外来着色：意料之中是暗的，出乎意料是亮的。<bookmark mark='b'/>再看同一段在2025年的Qwen3下的样子。它的方块几乎处处都更暗：350比特，而不是446比特。

cb6e29bf7eef.en: Look where they differ. <bookmark mark='a'/> After Bull, GPT-2 doesn't expect Durham, 7.4 bits, or tobacco, 9.4. Qwen3 does, 2.9 and 2.4: Bull Durham was a real brand of tobacco, and somewhere in its training it learned that. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the telephone: GPT-2 pays 11.0 bits for it, Qwen3 only 3.3, because two paragraphs earlier, a telephone bell rang. <bookmark mark='c'/> Show Qwen3 this paragraph on its own, and the telephone costs it 12.9 bits. It remembers: the long tail of the last chapter, put to use.
cb6e29bf7eef.zh: 看看它们在哪里不同。<bookmark mark='a'/>在Bull之后，GPT-2没料到Durham，7.4比特，也没料到“烟草”这个词，9.4比特。Qwen3都料到了，2.9和2.4：Bull Durham是一个真实的烟草品牌，它在训练中的某处学到了这一点。<bookmark mark='b'/>再看“电话”这个词：GPT-2为它付出11.0比特，Qwen3只要3.3比特，因为两段之前，一个电话铃响了。<bookmark mark='c'/>只给Qwen3看这一段，“电话”这个词就要花它12.9比特。它记得：上一章的长尾巴，在这里派上了用场。

bddfdda3acba.en: Facts work the same way. Ask for the city of the Eiffel Tower, <bookmark mark='a'/> the author of Pride and Prejudice, <bookmark mark='b'/> or the chemical symbol for gold, and the model that knows the answer pays far fewer bits when the answer comes. <bookmark mark='c'/> Arithmetic is harder: the 2025 model gives four 28 percent, but five 24.
bddfdda3acba.zh: 事实也是一样。问埃菲尔铁塔在哪座城市，<bookmark mark='a'/>问《傲慢与偏见》的作者是谁，<bookmark mark='b'/>或者问金的化学符号，知道答案的模型，在答案出现时花的比特要少得多。<bookmark mark='c'/>算术更难：2025年的模型给“four”的是28%，给“five”的却有24%。

eede5376c103.en: So here's the ladder. <bookmark mark='a'/> Letter frequencies get you 4.1 bits. Spelling, a few letters of context, gets you 2.0. <bookmark mark='b'/> Below that, a model has to learn words and grammar, facts about the world, and what has happened so far in the story, <bookmark mark='c'/> down toward the one bit or so that people need. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nobody tells the model to learn this. One number pushes it there: the bits it pays for each guess. To predict the text, it has to model the world that wrote it.
eede5376c103.zh: 所以，这就是阶梯。<bookmark mark='a'/>字母频率让你降到4.1比特。拼写，也就是几个字母的上下文，降到2.0。<bookmark mark='b'/>再往下，模型就得学会词和语法，关于世界的事实，以及故事到目前为止发生了什么，<bookmark mark='c'/>一直降向人所需要的大约1比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>没有人告诉模型去学这些。把它推到那里的，只是一个数：它为每次猜测付出的比特。要预测文本，它就得为写出这些文本的世界建模。

664a4c1d848b.en: Chapter fourteen. Before the final scores, a word about units.
664a4c1d848b.zh: 第14章。在最后的计分之前，先说说单位。

e2bf2d568882.en: Language models don't read letters. Each cuts text into tokens with its own vocabulary. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a paragraph of the Falcon passage as GPT-2 cuts it, <bookmark mark='b'/> and as Qwen3 does. <bookmark mark='c'/> Over the whole passage, GPT-2 needs 5,458 tokens, 3.92 characters each on average; Qwen3, with a bigger vocabulary, 5,217.
e2bf2d568882.zh: 语言模型读的不是字母。每个模型都用自己的词表，把文本切成词元。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是《马耳他之鹰》段落里的一段，按GPT-2的方式切开，<bookmark mark='b'/>再按Qwen3的方式切开。<bookmark mark='c'/>在整个段落上，GPT-2需要5458个词元，平均每个3.92个字符；Qwen3的词表更大，需要5217个。

63f2147f4d59.en: A model's loss is reported per token, so its size depends on how much text a token holds. <bookmark mark='a'/> What matters is the total: tokens times bits per token, which is characters times bits per character. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are our models on the passage; for the counting model, every token is a character. <bookmark mark='c'/> Per token, the counting model looks like the winner: 2.32 bits against GPT-2's 4.57, a perplexity of 5.0 against 23.8. But its tokens are single characters. Per character, it is 2.0 times worse. <bookmark mark='d'/> Perplexity, two to the bits per token, has the same problem: tokens differ. <bookmark mark='e'/> So compare per character, or per byte: that's why the scoreboard counts bits per character.
63f2147f4d59.zh: 模型的损失是按每个词元来报告的，所以它的大小取决于一个词元装了多少文本。<bookmark mark='a'/>要紧的是总数：词元数乘以每词元比特数，等于字符数乘以每字符比特数。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是我们的各个模型在这段文字上的成绩；对计数模型来说，每个词元就是一个字符。<bookmark mark='c'/>按词元算，计数模型看起来是赢家：2.32比特，对GPT-2的4.57；困惑度5.0，对23.8。可它的词元只是单个字符。按字符算，它差了2.0倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>困惑度，也就是2的每词元比特数次方，也有同样的问题：词元各不相同。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以要按每个字符，或者按每个字节来比：这就是为什么记分牌数的是每字符比特数。

699069a48abc.en: The field measures it this way too. In 2024, researchers at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Tencent took thirty-one public language models, <bookmark mark='a'/> measured how well each compresses freshly collected web pages, code and papers, in bits per character, since bits per token aren't comparable, <bookmark mark='b'/> and set that against their average score on twelve benchmarks of knowledge, coding and mathematics. <bookmark mark='c'/> The points fall almost on a line, with a correlation of minus 0.93. The better a model compresses, the more it can do.
699069a48abc.zh: 这个领域也是这样衡量的。2024年，香港科技大学和腾讯的研究者拿来31个公开的语言模型，<bookmark mark='a'/>测量每个模型压缩新收集的网页、代码和论文的本事，单位是每字符比特数，因为每词元比特数没法相互比较；<bookmark mark='b'/>再把它和这些模型在12个关于知识、编程和数学的基准测试上的平均分放在一起。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些点几乎落在一条直线上，相关系数是负0.93。一个模型压缩得越好，它能做的就越多。

4c131a60f582.en: Chapter fifteen. Time to keep score.

d096931c06eb.en: Next, the compressors on your computer. <bookmark mark='a'/> gzip, 3.31, xz, 3.20, bzip2, 2.92. They know nothing about English in advance, and learn only from the passage, as they go. <bookmark mark='b'/> Our best counting model, which read the thirty books first and looks at the previous 4 characters, gets 2.32.
d096931c06eb.zh: 接下来，是你电脑上的压缩器，每字符比特数依次是：<bookmark mark='a'/>gzip, 3.31, xz, 3.20, bzip2, 2.92。它们事先对英语一无所知，只从这段文字本身边读边学。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们最好的计数模型，先读了30本书，看前面4个字符，得到2.32。

0ccec5132a21.en: And then, the neural language models. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2, the smallest version, from 2019: 1.17 bits. Its largest version, 1.01. <bookmark mark='b'/> Qwen3, from 2025: the 0.6 billion parameter model already matches the largest GPT-2, <bookmark mark='c'/> and four billion parameters bring it to 0.87 bits per character. <bookmark mark='d'/> For comparison, Shannon's estimate for people, on letters alone, was 0.6 to 1.3.
0ccec5132a21.zh: 然后，是神经语言模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>2019年的GPT-2，最小的版本：1.17比特。它最大的版本，1.01。<bookmark mark='b'/>2025年的Qwen3：6亿参数的模型已经和最大的GPT-2持平，<bookmark mark='c'/>40亿参数把它降到每个字符0.87比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>作为对比，香农对人的估计，只算字母，是0.6到1.3。

10899f7d3cb2.en: The jump from counting, at 2.3 bits, to under one, is what this series is about: what these models learned, and how.
10899f7d3cb2.zh: 从计数的2.3比特，到1以下，这一跃就是这个系列要讲的：这些模型学到了什么，又是怎么学到的。

3c0c3b3e367c.en: Arithmetic coding turns any predictor into a compressor, so we built one. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2 small reads the start of the Falcon passage a token at a time, feeding chapter eight's 32-bit coder. Out come 688 bytes, 3.7 bits more than GPT-2's own surprise, <bookmark mark='b'/> and decoded it back, with a second run of the model, letter for letter. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the same 4,331 characters, xz needs 2,180 bytes: 3.2 times as many.
3c0c3b3e367c.zh: 算术编码能把任何一个预测者变成压缩器，所以我们造了一个。<bookmark mark='a'/>GPT-2 small一次一个词元地读《马耳他之鹰》段落的开头，把概率交给第8章那个32位编码器。出来的是688字节，只比GPT-2自己的意外度多3.7比特，<bookmark mark='b'/>再让模型重新跑一遍，把它一个字母不差地解码回来。<bookmark mark='c'/>同样这4331个字符，xz需要2180字节：是它的3.2倍。

88750bbcac22.en: There's a catch: the decompressor needs the model, and the model is big. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2 small squeezes the whole passage into 3.1 kilobytes, but its weights take 248 megabytes: count them, and the file is 11,572 times the passage. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2024, a DeepMind paper titled Language Modeling Is Compression put a 70-billion-parameter model on a gigabyte of Wikipedia: 8.3 percent of the original size, against 32 for gzip and 23 for xz; fourteen thousand percent, counting its weights. Trained on text, it also beat PNG and FLAC on images and audio. <bookmark mark='c'/> The Hutter Prize, started in 2006, counts everything: the record, set in July 2026, packs that gigabyte, decompressor included, into 100.4 megabytes, 0.80 bits per character, mixing many predictors. <bookmark mark='d'/> Prediction is compression, and the predictor's size is part of the bill.
88750bbcac22.zh: 这里有个问题：解压器需要模型，而模型很大。<bookmark mark='a'/>GPT-2 small把整段文字压到3.1KB，可它的权重要占248MB：把权重算进去，文件是这段文字的11572倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>2024年，DeepMind一篇题为《语言建模就是压缩》的论文，用一个700亿参数的模型压缩1GB的维基百科：压到原来大小的8.3%，而gzip是32%，xz是23%；把它的权重算进去，就是14000%。尽管是在文本上训练的，它压缩图像和音频也胜过PNG和FLAC。<bookmark mark='c'/>赫特奖设立于2006年，它把一切都算进去：2026年7月创下的纪录，把那1GB连同解压器一起，装进100.4MB，每个字符0.80比特，靠的是把许多预测者混合起来。<bookmark mark='d'/>预测就是压缩，而预测者本身的大小，也是账单的一部分。

0533afbf73a5.en: And the board isn't finished: <bookmark mark='a'/> better counting in Part 7, <bookmark mark='b'/> a neural network in Part 9, <bookmark mark='c'/> a network with memory in Part 10, <bookmark mark='d'/> and our own small transformer in Part 13, all trained on these books and scored on this page.
0533afbf73a5.zh: 记分牌还没写完：<bookmark mark='a'/>第7部分有更好的计数，<bookmark mark='b'/>第9部分有一个神经网络，<bookmark mark='c'/>第10部分有一个带记忆的网络，<bookmark mark='d'/>第13部分有我们自己的小Transformer，都在这些书上训练，在这一页上打分。

09a79f735251.en: Let's take stock. Guesses are probability distributions; the chain rule scores a whole text. Surprise had to be a logarithm, and entropy is the only consistent measure of uncertainty. Kraft's budget bounds every code, Huffman's is the best, and long typical sequences reach the entropy, no further. A wrong model costs the cross-entropy. Arithmetic coding made predicting and compressing one thing, and GPT-2 compressed our passage and decoded it back, letter for letter. Counting taught generalization by failing at it, and mutual information showed how far back text remembers.
09a79f735251.zh: 我们来盘点一下。猜测就是概率分布；链式法则给一整段文本打分。意外度必须是对数，而熵是唯一自洽的不确定性度量。克拉夫特的预算约束着每一个编码，霍夫曼编码是其中最好的，而长的典型序列能达到熵，却不能更低。错误的模型要付出交叉熵的代价。算术编码让预测和压缩成了同一回事，GPT-2压缩了我们的段落，又一个字母不差地把它解码了回来。计数用失败教会了我们泛化，互信息则告诉我们，文本能记住多远的过去。

d2dcccbebaf1.en: Almost everything here comes back. The chain rule is how language models generate text, and how reasoning models think out loud. Cross-entropy is the loss we'll minimize for the rest of the series. The divergence's two directions return in variational autoencoders and in alignment. Drawing typical text from a model is Part 5. And compression returns with scaling, and at the very end, when we ask what these models can be trusted with.
d2dcccbebaf1.zh: 这里的几乎每一样都会再次出现。链式法则是语言模型生成文本的方式，也是推理模型把思考说出来的方式。交叉熵是我们在整个系列里要一直最小化的损失。散度的两个方向，会在变分自编码器和对齐里再次出现。从模型中抽取典型的文本，在第5部分。压缩会在研究规模时回来，也会在最后，当我们问这些模型能被托付什么时回来。

0855b12ef326.en: Here are six problems to try, from the grouping rule to Laplace's rule of succession. Pause here and work through them; full solutions are in this part's notes.
0855b12ef326.zh: 这里有六道题，从分组法则到拉普拉斯接续法则。在这里暂停，把它们做一做；完整的解答在这一部分的笔记里。

cbcfeadf713b.en: Next time: the other road to intelligence, the one that came first. Alan Turing's question; machines that search, uniformly, <bookmark mark='a'/> or guided toward a goal; programs that play games and prove theorems; the expert systems; and the winters that followed. The symbolic era.
cbcfeadf713b.zh: 下一次：通向智能的另一条路，也是更早出现的那一条。艾伦·图灵的问题；会搜索的机器，一视同仁地搜，<bookmark mark='a'/>或者朝着目标有引导地搜；会下棋、会证明定理的程序；专家系统；以及随之而来的寒冬。符号主义时代。

be8ceda9675a.en: This part followed the first chapters of Cover and Thomas's Elements of Information Theory, and MacKay's Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms, both of which go much further. The papers are all worth reading, starting with Shannon's two. Thanks for watching, and see you in Part 2.
be8ceda9675a.zh: 这一部分沿着科弗和托马斯的《信息论基础》，以及麦凯的《信息论、推理与学习算法》的前几章展开，两本书都走得远得多。这些论文都值得一读，先从香农的那两篇开始。感谢观看，第2部分见。

0763b3eb93d9.en: From those frequencies, the rank entropy is 2.37 bits per letter: an estimate of the upper bound. <bookmark mark='a'/> Shannon's lower-bound expression gives 1.36, but its proof assumes an ideal guesser, ranking letters by their true conditional probabilities. Our counting program is not ideal, so that lower endpoint is illustrative, not a certified bound.
0763b3eb93d9.zh: 根据这些频率，猜测次数的熵是每个字母2.37比特，这是对上界的一个估计。<bookmark mark='a'/>香农的下界表达式算出1.36，但它的证明假设猜测者是理想的，按真正的条件概率给字母排序。我们的计数程序并不理想，所以这个下端点只是演示，不是有保证的下界。

f22f712379b5.en: Shannon's own subjects did far better. <bookmark mark='a'/> With a hundred letters of context, he put printed English between 0.6 and 1.3 bits per letter, <bookmark mark='b'/> against a rank entropy of 2.4 for our counting guesser with six. Its lower endpoint is only illustrative, and Shannon also cautioned about sampling error and imperfect human guessing. <bookmark mark='c'/> The difference is knowledge: of words and grammar, idioms, the story, and how the world works.
f22f712379b5.zh: 香农自己的受试者做得好得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>给他们100个字母的上下文，他估计印刷英语每个字母是0.6到1.3比特，<bookmark mark='b'/>而我们用6个字母上下文的计数程序，猜测次数的熵是2.4。它的下端点只是演示；香农也提醒过，采样误差和人类猜测的不完美都会影响估计。<bookmark mark='c'/>差别在于知识：关于词和语法、习语、故事，以及世界是怎么运转的知识。

307ffe9422a2.en: Here's the board, for the Falcon passage as printed: capitals, punctuation, everything. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plain text spends about eight bits per character. <bookmark mark='b'/> The passage uses only 61 different symbols, so a blind guess among them costs 5.93 bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Letter frequencies, counted in our thirty books, bring it to 4.55, <bookmark mark='d'/> and one character of context, to 3.58.
307ffe9422a2.zh: 这是记分牌，针对印刷原样的《马耳他之鹰》段落：大写、标点，什么都在。<bookmark mark='a'/>纯文本每个字符大约花8比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>这段文字只用了61种不同的符号，所以在它们之间盲猜，要花5.93比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们30本书里数出的字母频率，把它降到4.55，<bookmark mark='d'/>一个字符的上下文，降到3.58。

7042a8de10bc.en: And we'll keep score. Here is a page of The Maltese Falcon, from 1930. Its Project Gutenberg edition appeared in January 2026. We hold it out of the models we train here. For pretrained models, earlier copies may have been in their training data. <bookmark mark='a'/> As plain text, it takes about eight bits per character. <bookmark mark='b'/> The series explains how the numbers on this board come down: from eight, to below one.
7042a8de10bc.zh: 我们还要记分。这是1930年的《马耳他之鹰》里的一页。它的古登堡计划版本在2026年1月发布。我们自己训练的模型不读这段文字；但预训练模型的训练数据里，可能有过更早的版本。<bookmark mark='a'/>存成纯文本，每个字符大约要8比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个系列要解释的，就是记分牌上的这些数字是怎么降下来的：从8，降到1以下。
